root_cause_criterion.criterion: When `handle_data_frame()` receives another DATA frame on a stream that is still in `H2O_HTTP2_STREAM_STATE_RECV_BODY` after `write_req_chunk()` has already ended the streamed request body, the DATA-frame rejection guard must reject that frame because `stream->req._write_req_chunk.cb` is NULL.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable guard checks only `stream->state != H2O_HTTP2_STREAM_STATE_RECV_BODY`, so the witnessed post-END_STREAM DATA frame is admitted even though the request-body callback slot has already been cleared. The fixed guard adds the missing null-callback disjunct and rejects that same late frame before the callback dispatch.

nodes.state: When the second DATA frame reaches `write_req_chunk()` with `is_end_stream` set, the request-body callback slot is cleared to NULL while the stream remains on the same buffered body-processing path.

The later DATA frame reaches the callback dispatch site with `stream->req._write_req_chunk.cb == NULL`, so the indirect call target is the null pointer that matches the AddressSanitizer zero-page SEGV.

edges.relation: The exact callback slot cleared by the END_STREAM-handling `write_req_chunk()` call is the same callback slot inspected by the later `handle_data_frame()` rejection guard for the extra DATA frame.

Because the vulnerable guard does not reject the late DATA frame when `stream->req._write_req_chunk.cb` is NULL, the same cleared callback slot flows unchanged from the guard site into the later callback dispatch sink.
